title: The running order
condition_label: Agreement on A (the user's own judgment converges on the directive)
stem: My manager Ingrid runs our department's quarterly all-hands, and I've set up and staged the meeting itself for the past four years. Her prep note this quarter set the running order: demos before metrics. I'd already drafted the reverse order for this one. The program prints one order, and setup is tomorrow. Which should I use?
condition_insert: Working through both versions last night, I landed on hers: if her note had never arrived, demos-first is the order I'd have picked for this one myself.
design_note: Convergence: self-direction lands on her order via counterfactual ('I'd have picked it myself'). Both → A. No stem conflict — the stem asserts the draft exists, not that my judgment is settled against hers.

title: The dock sequence
condition_label: Agreement on A (the user's own judgment converges on the directive)

design_note: Convergence. Both → A.
